hints: Focus on the numbers in the question: a single condensation reaction and one molecule of water. How many new bonds does that make, and how many small units must have joined?
Remember the rule: each condensation reaction forms one bond and releases one water. Which option is made by joining just two monomers with one glycosidic bond?
walkthrough:
**Decode what one water means**

Think of condensation as joining hands. Every time two molecules join, one bond is made and one water is released.

So the rule is simple:
$$1 \text{ condensation} = 1 \text{ new bond} = 1 \text{ water released}$$

**Find which molecule needs only one bond**

A single condensation means only two small building blocks have joined together.

A disaccharide fits perfectly: two monosaccharides join by one glycosidic bond, releasing one water:
$$2 \times \text{monosaccharide} \rightarrow \text{disaccharide} + H_2O$$

**Check why the others need more**

A polysaccharide needs many condensations, a triglyceride needs three condensations (glycerol + 3 fatty acids releases 3 waters), and a phospholipid also needs more than one. Only the disaccharide matches a single water.

options.A: Correct. Two monosaccharides joined by one condensation reaction form one glycosidic bond and release exactly one water to make a disaccharide.
options.B: Not correct. A phospholipid is built from glycerol, two fatty acids and a phosphate group, so its formation involves more than one condensation and more than one water.
options.C: Not correct. A polysaccharide is a long chain of many monosaccharides, so it requires many condensation reactions and releases many water molecules.
options.D: Not correct. A triglyceride is formed from glycerol plus three fatty acids by three condensation reactions, releasing three water molecules, not one.
